key_insight: Severe plastic deformation strengthens CrMnFeCoNi while unusually increasing electrical and thermal conductivity, with inferred phonon transport gains exceeding electron transport gains.
engineering_relevance: Defect engineering could help tune strength and heat transport together in high-entropy alloys rather than imposing the usual conductivity penalty.
method: Apply high-pressure torsion for up to four turns to generate hierarchical defects and nanostructure.
Measure hardness, electrical and thermal conductivity, heat capacity, and thermal expansion.
Analyze transport using the Wiedemann–Franz law and Cahill–Pohl minimum-conductivity model.
evidence_signal: After four turns, electrical conductivity rose from 0.953 to 1.003 ± 0.005 MS/m and thermal conductivity from 10.3 to 14.4 W/(m·K), while hardness saturated near 520 Hv.
watch_item: Deformation-induced short-range ordering is a proposed explanation, not an established mechanism, and electron–phonon transport separation is model-dependent.
paper_title: Unusual increase in electrical and thermal conductivity of severely deformed CrMnFeCoNi high-entropy alloy: Roles of disordering and nanostructuring in electron and phonon transport
